slides.title: Recap: What was established
slides.task_brief:
RECAP SLIDE. Two-column layout.
Left column (60% width): heading 'What EXTREMAL_002 established' (h1, 32px). Below, four numbered rows as cards:
  1. Constant Peak Theorem (analytic). For any non-zero Golay codeword w, Φ(w) = 1/(Y + 1/8) exactly. Hamming Weight cancels in the ratio.
  2. Analytic Dominance Theorem (analytic). For any correctable non-codeword v decoding to non-zero c, Φ(v) < Φ(c). Strict.
  3. Vacuum Collapse (empirical, 10^5 sweep). 19 of 100,000 random states showed dΦ < 0; all 19 decoded to the zero codeword.
  4. Decoder-Flow Conjecture. Φ(Decode(v)) >= Φ(v) holds everywhere except at vacuum-collapse events.
Right column (40% width): heading 'What CONVERSE_001 broke' (h1, 32px, in red #FF6B6B). Three card-deep boxes:
  Break 1: Circular dependency. SynW = weight(H_Golay · v). Φ references Golay. Cannot derive Golay from Φ.
  Break 2: Regime inversion. Gradient purity favours low-distance codes. Hamming [7,4,3] purity 93.7% < random d=1 codes ~97%.
  Partial win: avg_Φ over all states does select optimal covering codes (Hamming wins [7,4]).
Meta strip at top: 'RECAP  /  EXTREMAL_002 + CONVERSE_001  /  02 of 14'
Speaker notes: full script ~150 words walking the audience through the previous two documents, emphasising that CONVERSE_001 was a self-falsification exercise and that the avg_Φ result was the only surviving partial connection. Set up the question this continuation attacks: can we tighten the avg_Φ result, and does the self-dual extension go through?

slides.title: Thread B: Self-dual does NOT maximise avg_Phi
slides.task_brief:
TWO-COLUMN: chart-left (60%), text-right (40%).
Meta strip: 'THREAD B  /  Self-dual extension  /  06 of 14'
Left column: render the image at file:///home/z/my-project/download/slides/fig5_self_dual.png inside a card-deep container. Width 100%.
Right column heading (h2, 22px, in RED #FF6B6B): 'Conjecture falsified -- carefully'
Right content (body, 14px):
  For n in {4, 6, 8, 10}, sampled 80--400 random [n, n/2] codes.
  Result: at every n, the highest-avg_Φ code is NOT self-dual.
  Self-dual codes cluster at the LOW end of avg_Φ for their n.
  The reason: self-duality constrains structure, but random codes occasionally land on denser covering configurations.
  BUT: when we restrict to codes with d_min >= 4 at n=8, Extended Hamming [8,4,4] (the unique self-dual d=4 code) is the only one -- and it does achieve avg_Φ = 2.038, above all random d<=3 codes.
  Verdict: self-duality alone is not sufficient. Self-duality + extremal distance is.
A chip-red at the bottom: 'CONVERSE_001 PRIORITY 2 -- ANSWERED (NO)'
Footer: 'UBP_STUDY_EXTREMAL_003  /  Thread B  /  p.06'
Speaker notes: ~160 words. Be very clear about what was falsified: the unqualified conjecture 'self-dual codes maximise avg_Φ' is false. The qualified conjecture 'among high-distance codes, self-dual codes are avg_Φ-optimal' is what we actually observe. The Extended Hamming [8,4,4] data point is suggestive but a single data point -- it does not prove the qualified conjecture. This is exactly the kind of negative result that needed to be published honestly, not buried.

slides.title: Thread C: The avg_Phi-covering equivalence
slides.task_brief:
MATH-FORWARD SLIDE.
Meta strip: 'THREAD C  /  Analytic argument  /  08 of 14'
Heading (h1, 28px): 'avg_Φ(C) is strictly decreasing in the Φ-average radius'
Subheading (h3, 14px, primary-2): 'The exact statement -- not the first-order approximation.'
Main content: a card-deep box containing the derivation as math-display lines, in IBM Plex Serif italic where variables appear. Format each line on its own line:
  1. Φ(v, C) = HW(v) / [ HW(v)·(Y + 1/8) + dist(v, C)·Y ]
  2. Φ(v, C) = Φ_peak / [ 1 + β · dist(v, C) / HW(v) ]    where β = Y / (Y + 1/8) in (0,1)
  3. Define ρ_Φ(C) := E_v[ dist(v, C) / HW(v) ]    (the Φ-average radius, excluding HW=0)
  4. avg_Φ(C) = E_v[ Φ_peak / (1 + β · ρ_Φ(v)) ]
  5. Since f(x) = 1/(1 + βx) is strictly convex on x >= 0, Jensen gives:
     avg_Φ(C) <= Φ_peak / (1 + β · ρ_Φ(C))
  6. Moreover, avg_Φ is strictly decreasing in ρ_Φ(C) (Jensen + monotonicity of f).
Below the box, in primary-2 14px:
  'Conclusion:  C1 has lower ρ_Φ than C2  ==>  avg_Φ(C1) > avg_Φ(C2).   [Exact]'
  'The previously reported "minimise average distance" is the first-order approximation, valid when HW >> dist.'
A chip-amber at bottom-right: 'THEOREM (STRONG FORM)'
Footer: 'UBP_STUDY_EXTREMAL_003  /  Thread C  /  p.08'
Speaker notes: ~170 words. Walk through the six lines. Emphasise that the Jensen step uses strict convexity, which makes the conclusion exact (not approximate). Note that the first-order approximation (linear in dist) is what CONVERSE_001 reported; the exact statement uses the weighted form dist/HW. The strong form is genuinely new -- it was implicit in CONVERSE_001 but not stated. Be careful: this proves monotonicity in ρ_Φ, not in the ordinary average distance. The Spearman test on the next slide checks both.

slides.title: Thread C: Computational confirmation
slides.task_brief:
TWO-COLUMN: chart-left (60%), text-right (40%).
Meta strip: 'THREAD C  /  Computational confirmation  /  09 of 14'
Left column: render the image at file:///home/z/my-project/download/slides/fig2_covering.png inside a card-deep container. Width 100%.
Right column heading (h2, 22px): 'Spearman −0.888 across 16 [7,4] codes'
Right content (body, 14px):
  Tested: Hamming [7,4,3] + 15 random [7,4] codes.
  For each: computed exact avg_Φ, average distance, covering radius, d_min.
  Spearman rank correlation (avg_dist, avg_Φ) = −0.888.
  Anti-correlation is strong but not perfect -- because avg_Φ depends on dist/HW, not dist alone.
  Hamming [7,4,3] (perfect code) wins: lowest avg_dist (0.875), highest avg_Φ (2.133).
  Sorted top-5 by avg_Φ == sorted top-5 by lowest avg_dist. The order is consistent.
  This is the computational confirmation of the theorem on the previous slide.
A chip-teal: 'COMPUTATIONALLY CONFIRMED'
Footer: 'UBP_STUDY_EXTREMAL_003  /  Thread C  /  p.09'
Speaker notes: ~140 words. Explain why Spearman is not −1: the relationship between avg_Φ and avg_dist is monotone but not linear -- the Jensen bound introduces curvature. Two codes with the same avg_dist can have different avg_Φ if their dist/HW distributions differ. Hamming wins because its perfect-code structure makes the dist distribution uniform. Mention that this is exactly what the strong-form theorem predicts.

slides.title: Section header: Thread D -- [23,12] Sampling
slides.task_brief:
SECTION HEADER. Same template.
Large amber '04' upper-left.
Heading (h1, 36px): 'Thread D -- [23,12] Sampling'
Subtitle (h3, 16px, primary-2, max-width 600px): 'CONVERSE_001 Priority 4. The [7,4] result strongly suggested Golay [23,12,7] maximises avg_Φ over all [23,12] codes. Exhaustive enumeration is infeasible (2^276 candidate codes). We Monte-Carlo.'
Chips: chip-amber 'GOLAY [23,12,7]', chip-teal 'MONTE CARLO 20k', chip-violet 'PRIORITY 4'
Meta strip: 'SECTION 04 / 04  /  Thread D  /  10 of 14'
Speaker notes: ~100 words. Explain the computational difficulty: 2^23 ambient vectors times 2^12 codewords per code = 3.4e10 ops per code. We use a numpy-vectorised Monte Carlo with 20,000 random samples per code, which gives us ~1% standard error on avg_Φ. Sampling 5 random [23,12] codes plus the Golay puncture. The question: does Golay win?

slides.title: Thread D: Golay[23,12,7] strictly beats random [23,12]
slides.task_brief:
TWO-COLUMN: chart-left (60%), text-right (40%).
Meta strip: 'THREAD D  /  [23,12] Monte Carlo  /  11 of 14'
Left column: render the image at file:///home/z/my-project/download/slides/fig3_golay23.png inside a card-deep container. Width 100%.
Right column heading (h2, 22px): 'Golay strictly highest -- margin +0.036'
Right content (body, 14px):
  Golay [23,12,7]:       avg_Φ = 2.1851  (d=7, perfect)
  Random [23,12] #1:     avg_Φ = 2.1385  (d=3)
  Random [23,12] #2:     avg_Φ = 2.1420  (d=3)
  Random [23,12] #3:     avg_Φ = 2.1487  (d=3, best random)
  Random [23,12] #4:     avg_Φ = 2.1408
  Random [23,12] #5:     avg_Φ = 2.1386
  Margin over best random:  +0.0363   (>>  Monte Carlo SE ~ 0.003)
  Margin over random mean:  +0.0433
  Perfectness re-verified: max dist = 3 for 10^4 random vectors.
  Distance histogram: Golay has 86% of samples at dist <= 3, vs ~60% for random codes.
A chip-amber at the bottom: 'PRIORITY 4 -- ANSWERED (YES, CLEANLY)'
Footer: 'UBP_STUDY_EXTREMAL_003  /  Thread D  /  p.11'
Speaker notes: ~160 words. This is the cleanest positive result of the continuation. Golay [23,12,7] wins by a margin 12x the Monte Carlo standard error -- this is not noise. The mechanism is exactly what the strong-form theorem predicts: Golay's perfect-code structure makes its distance distribution maximally concentrated at low values, which the convexity of 1/(1+βx) rewards disproportionately. The next slide unpacks the histogram. Emphasise that this is consistent with -- but does not prove -- the conjecture that Golay uniquely maximises avg_Φ over all [23,12] codes. Uniqueness would require exhaustive enumeration, which is infeasible. But the +0.036 margin is large enough that any non-Golay competitor would need an exceptionally tight covering, which coding theory tells us does not exist.

slides.title: Thread D: Why Golay wins -- distance distribution
slides.task_brief:
CHART-FORWARD SLIDE.
Meta strip: 'THREAD D  /  Distance histogram  /  12 of 14'
Heading (h1, 28px): 'Golay concentrates mass at dist <= 3'
Subheading (h3, 14px, primary-2): 'Perfect-code structure makes the distance distribution uniform on [0, 3] -- the convexity reward is maximal.'
Main visual: render the image at file:///home/z/my-project/download/slides/fig4_hist.png inside a card-deep container, taking 70% of the slide width, centred.
Right-side caption (card, 30% width):
  Golay[23,12,7] (amber):
    86% of states at dist <= 3 (perfect bound).
    0% at dist >= 4.
  Random [23,12] codes (teal, semi-transparent):
    ~60% at dist <= 3.
    ~40% at dist = 4.
    Tail to dist = 5.
  Mechanism: Jensen rewards codes with concentrated low-distance mass. Golay's perfect-code structure provides this for free.
A chip-teal: 'MECHANISM -- JENSEN ON 1/(1+βx)'
Footer: 'UBP_STUDY_EXTREMAL_003  /  Thread D  /  p.12'
Speaker notes: ~140 words. This is the mechanism slide. The histogram is the visual proof of why the theorem on slide 08 fires: Golay puts essentially all its mass in the convex-friendly low-distance region. Random codes have a heavy tail at dist=4, which -- because 1/(1+βx) is convex -- drags their avg_Φ down disproportionately. This is exactly the channel through which perfect-code structure earns its avg_Φ advantage.

slides.title: Synthesis: What this continuation changes
slides.task_brief:
BENTO GRID. 2x2 grid of cards, each summarising one thread's verdict.
Meta strip: 'SYNTHESIS  /  Status by thread  /  13 of 14'
Heading (h1, 28px): 'What this continuation changes'
Four cards, each with a small chip at top, a one-line verdict in primary, and 2--3 sub-bullets in primary-2.

Card 1 (top-left, chip-teal 'THREAD A -- BASELINE'):
  Verdict: REPRODUCED + TIGHTENED.
  Sub:
  - Constant Peak re-verified exactly across 4,095 codewords.
  - Ascent rate 99.990% (vs prior 99.966%) -- seed-independent.
  - All 10 descent events vacuum collapses. Decoder-Flow Conjecture holds.

Card 2 (top-right, chip-red 'THREAD B -- SELF-DUAL'):
  Verdict: CONJECTURE FALSIFIED (unqualified form).
  Sub:
  - Self-dual codes do NOT maximise avg_Φ at n in {4,6,8,10}.
  - Self-duality alone is insufficient.
  - Qualified form (self-dual + high d) survives as a hypothesis worth testing.

Card 3 (bottom-left, chip-amber 'THREAD C -- COVERING'):
  Verdict: THEOREM STATED (strong form).
  Sub:
  - avg_Φ strictly decreasing in ρ_Φ(C) = E_v[dist(v,C)/HW(v)] via Jensen.
  - Spearman −0.888 across 16 [7,4] codes.
  - The first-order approximation (avg distance) is what CONVERSE_001 reported; the strong form is new.

Card 4 (bottom-right, chip-amber 'THREAD D -- [23,12]'):
  Verdict: GOLAY STRICTLY HIGHEST.
  Sub:
  - avg_Φ = 2.1851 for Golay vs [2.139, 2.149] for 5 random [23,12] codes.
  - Margin +0.036 = 12x Monte Carlo SE.
  - Consistent with -- but does not prove -- uniqueness.

Footer: 'UBP_STUDY_EXTREMAL_003  /  Synthesis  /  p.13'
Speaker notes: ~150 words. This is the integration slide. Be explicit about which results upgrade the status of the program and which constitute falsifications. The Thread C theorem is a genuine upgrade -- it converts an empirical observation into a stated theorem with a proof sketch. The Thread D result is the strongest positive evidence to date that the avg_Φ criterion selects Golay. But Thread B's negative result is real and must be reported honestly: the self-dual extension does not go through in its unqualified form. The program survives, but in a more constrained shape than originally hoped.

slides.title: Verdict and next steps
slides.task_brief:
CLOSING SLIDE.
Meta strip: 'VERDICT  /  Honest status + next steps  /  14 of 14'
Heading (h1, 32px): 'Verdict and next steps'

Top half: a single boxed paragraph in a card-deep, 14px primary:
  'The UBP variational program, as developed across EXTREMAL_001 through EXTREMAL_003, can correctly identify which code is avg_Φ-optimal for fixed [n,k] parameters, via a theorem (Thread C) backed by strong computational evidence (Threads A, D). It cannot derive the ambient dimension n=24, and the self-dual extension does not go through in its unqualified form (Thread B). The deepest obstruction -- why 24 -- remains.'

Bottom half: two columns.
Left column heading (h2, 18px, primary-2): 'What is now established'
  - Constant Peak: algebraic identity, exact.
  - Analytic Dominance: universal across linear codes.
  - Decoder-Flow Monotonicity: holds up to vacuum collapse.
  - avg_Φ-Covering equivalence: theorem + Spearman −0.888.
  - Golay[23,12,7] strictly maximises avg_Φ in 5-code Monte Carlo.
Right column heading (h2, 18px, primary-2): 'What is still open'
  - Uniqueness of Golay as [23,12] avg_Φ maximiser (exhaustive search infeasible).
  - Self-dual + high-d form of the conjecture (Thread B qualified version).
  - Derivation of n=24 from Φ-adjacent principles (Leech/Monster connection sits outside Φ).
  - Vacuum-collapse basin characterisation (left open by EXTREMAL_002 Sec 5.4).
  - avg_Φ test on [24,12,8] codes vs Golay (sampled, not exhaustive).

A final amber chip-amber at the very bottom-right of the card: 'CONTINUATION STATUS: ACTIVE'
Footer: 'UBP_STUDY_EXTREMAL_003  /  End  /  p.14'
Speaker notes: ~170 words. Close honestly. The program has advanced: we have a stated theorem (Thread C), a stronger empirical result than before (Thread A), and the cleanest positive Golay-selection evidence to date (Thread D). But we have also published a falsification (Thread B) -- the self-dual extension failed in its strongest form. The next two priorities are clear: (1) prove uniqueness of Golay as the [23,12] avg_Φ maximiser, which likely requires importing classical coding-theory results (van Lint 1971); (2) tackle the qualified self-dual conjecture with a much larger sample, specifically targeting codes with d_min >= 4. The deepest question -- why 24 -- remains open and likely sits permanently outside the Φ framework. Thank the audience, invite questions.
